body:
Looking at this code, I'm not sure this is a great idea, performance wise.

The way it is implemented here involves a lot of runtime overhead: Creating new vectors, string checks, callbacks, etc.
Normally, I'd suggest that swizzling should be completely resolved at compile time, which would make it possible to compile swizzled access without much overhead in almost all cases (e.g. `vector.yx = [a, b]` can compile to `vector.y = a; vector.x = b`), avoiding all the parsing and allocations at runtime.

However, in GDScript we always have to deal with gradual typing, which means that swizzling would bleed into normal member access: If anything is accessing a member by anyone, we always have to check if it's a "swizzled access" because we weren't able to check this at compile time. Besides the additional overhead for _every single member access_ (including non-swizzled), an actual swizzle would incur the cost of runtime resolution, which would be very noticeable.

Overall I'm not convinced this is worth it.

I haven't followed discussions around replacing swizzles with "member-like access", e.g. `vector2.yx` is a "special member" on `Vector2` with a custom getter and custom setter taking and returning `Vector2`. This would alleviate most of my concerns. 
But I see you have rejected this possibility in the OP, so I'm guessing this was discussed and rejected before too.
